Job Description

The Role:

Conduct original research and develop practical AI/ML methods that accelerate GM’s research, engineering, and product development capabilities. This role is intended for a recent or soon-to-be-completed Ph.D. who brings strong depth in one or more advanced AI areas and the ability to work across disciplines. The intern will develop proof-of-concepts (POCs), evaluate them on meaningful engineering or scientific problems, communicate findings clearly, and collaborate with senior researchers and engineering partners to move promising ideas toward impact.

The Team:

GM R&D is seeking an outstanding early-career intern to contribute to advanced work in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Large Language Models. The role is designed for a fresh Ph.D. It emphasizes research depth, originality, experimental rigor, and growth toward independent technical leadership. The successful candidate will work with senior researchers, technical fellows, and engineering collaborators to formulate important problems, develop new methods, build research prototypes, and validate results. The work may span causal reasoning, neurosymbolic AI, world models, multimodal and generative AI, engineering agents, or related areas. The intern will be expected to connect theory and experimentation with real engineering needs while maintaining high standards for reproducibility, explainability, uncertainty awareness, and responsible AI.

What You’ll Do:

• Conduct original research in one or more advanced AI areas such as causal AI, neurosymbolic AI, world models, multimodal or generative AI or engineering agents.

• Translate engineering and scientific challenges into well-defined research questions, hypotheses, algorithms, and experimental plans.

• Design, implement, and evaluate machine learning models and proof-of-concepts using real, simulated, experimental, or engineering data.

• Develop methods that can reason about physical systems, causal relationships, uncertainty, constraints, temporal evolution, or complex interactions among components.

• Establish meaningful baselines and evaluation protocols; analyze failure modes, robustness, generalization, interpretability, and uncertainty rather than relying only on headline accuracy.

• Build reproducible research code, data-processing workflows, and experiment pipelines using modern deep learning practices.

• Collaborate with GM R&D researchers and engineering partners to understand domain constraints, validate research results, and identify pathways from POCs to practical use.

• Communicate technical findings through research reports, presentations, publications, invention disclosures, demonstrations, and clear documentation.

• Contribute to technical discussions and research roadmaps by identifying promising approaches, important risks, and high-value experiments.

• Participate in a collaborative research culture that values intellectual curiosity, constructive peer review, responsible innovation, and continuous learning.

More About Who You Are

• A curious and intellectually rigorous researcher who enjoys working on difficult, open-ended problems.

• Deeply grounded in at least one technical area, while eager to learn and collaborate across adjacent AI, computational science, and engineering disciplines.

• Motivated by research that can create measurable value in real-world engineering workflows, not only benchmark performance.

• Comfortable moving between mathematical formulation, algorithm development, software implementation, and empirical validation.

• Able to explain complex ideas, assumptions, limitations, and results to both technical and general audiences.

• Independent in driving research tasks to completion while actively seeking feedback and working effectively with senior mentors and cross-functional teams.

• Committed to careful experimentation, reproducibility, safety, explainability, and responsible use of AI.

Required Qualifications:

- Pursuit of a PhD in one of the following areas: Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Computational Science, Engineering, Physics, or a related field.

- Must be a current student

- Able to work fulltime, 40 hours per week during the summer months
- Demonstrated research depth in at least one relevant area, supported by a dissertation, publications, patents, open-source work, research software, or comparable technical contributions.
- Strong foundations in machine learning and deep learning, with working knowledge of optimization, probability/statistics, numerical methods, or scientific computing as appropriate to the research area.
- Experience developing and evaluating models in Python and frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow, or comparable tools.
- Ability to formulate experiments, select appropriate metrics and baselines, analyze results, and communicate technical conclusions with appropriate caveats.
- Strong verbal and written communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with researchers, engineers, and technical stakeholders.
- Ability to work on-site or in a hybrid research environment in accordance with GM work practices and project needs.

Preferred Qualifications:

- Research experience in causal inference, counterfactual reasoning, neurosymbolic methods and world models for engineering applications.
- Experience with multimodal AI, large language models, agentic systems, retrieval and reasoning, or AI-assisted engineering and software development.
- Evidence of research impact through high-quality publications, patents, invention disclosures, open-source contributions, awards, or successful technology demonstrations.
- Research or internship experience in automotive, mobility, aerospace, industrial, energy, defense, national laboratory, or university-industry collaboration settings.

About the role

Dedalus Labs builds persistent computers for AI agents. Our flagship product, Dedalus Machines, gives agents an isolated environment where they can run software, keep files and state, and work over time.

You'll implement and debug the software that creates, schedules, and runs Machines. Projects can involve the control plane, Kubernetes controllers and operators, or our Rust virtual machine monitor (VMM), the software that runs virtual machines. We want someone curious about how a system behaves when requests overlap, a node fails, or a process stops halfway through an operation.

About the internship

This is an evergreen opening. We review applications on an ongoing basis. Internships and co-ops last 3-9 months, depending on your school and co-op program.

Show us that you can learn something difficult, finish a working version, and improve it when the first approach fails. Prior production ownership is not required. You should be able to explain your project’s hardest bug, limits, and your contribution.

Work you might take on

- Kubernetes and orchestration: Improve a controller or operator and test how it reconciles desired and actual resource state. Investigate scheduling, pod lifecycle, networking, or recovery after a node failure.

- Control-plane correctness: Fix a resource-lifecycle bug involving retries, cancellation, concurrent requests, or cleanup. Write a test that reproduces the failure and verifies the repair.

- Runtime and storage: Improve VM startup, snapshot restore, memory use, or an I/O path. Establish a baseline and measure the change on the same workload.

- Failure testing: Inject a process crash, delayed response, or interrupted operation to expose an ordering or recovery assumption. Explain which guarantees the test establishes.

Finish with tested code, an explanation of your decisions, and a handoff another engineer can use.

What we look for

You can build and debug software in Rust, Go, C, C++, or a similar language. Rust is preferred for runtime work. You understand the memory, concurrency, data structures, and operating-system behavior your project depends on.

Kubernetes experience is especially relevant to control-plane work: controllers, operators, reconciliation, scheduling, networking, and resource lifecycles. For runtime work, relevant projects include a storage engine, networking tool, virtual machine, compiler, or operating-system component. Depth in either area is welcome.

Coursework, research, employment, open source, and independent projects all count. Explain what you personally implemented and learned. Experience at a big tech company or on another large, fast-moving codebase is a plus, not a requirement.

You understand when to use unit, integration, end-to-end, and property-based tests, and what each can and cannot establish. You choose efficient ways to verify a change, test invariants and failure cases, and make failures reproducible. Experience with formal verification or model checking is a plus.

When stuck, you narrow the problem, read source or documentation, and run an informative experiment. You ask for help with evidence, act on feedback, and finish the work.

You can use AI tools. You must understand, test, and correct the code you submit.

This internship may be a poor fit if

- You want a tutorial with every implementation step supplied.

- You cannot explain or debug the code in the project you submit.

- You lose interest after the first successful run, before checking failure cases or documenting what remains incomplete.

Logistics

40 hours per week, five days onsite in San Francisco. Relocation assistance may be available. Strong interns may be considered for full-time roles.

Show us your work

Show us a controller, service, runtime, storage component, or other systems project you built, and a difficult correctness or performance problem you investigated. They can come from the same project. Use existing work.

- Work: Show the code, demo, design, or result. Explain what you personally owned, what you reused, and one decision that made the result better or simpler.

- Investigation: Describe the symptom, your first explanation, the evidence that changed your thinking, and how you established the result. Include the workload or users involved and any important limitations.

- Engineering judgment: Link a public PR or commit, by you or anyone else, that you find interesting. Explain why it is an example of quality software engineering in the context in which it was written.

- Writing: Share one piece of writing you care about as a separate, required sample. Any medium or length is welcome. Tell us why you wrote it, who it was for, and what you wanted to communicate. Looking back, what works well and what would you change? We care about the quality of your thinking and writing, and your reflection on the work. Link it or paste a redacted excerpt. Explain your contribution and any coauthors or AI assistance.

Employment, open source, research, coursework, and independent projects all count. Links to your technical work or existing demos are optional but highly recommended so we can evaluate your body of work. Redacted excerpts are welcome for private work.

Tell us which problem in this role you want to own and why.

You can also explore our engineering tooling: Bessemer (BSMR) and Hollywood.

Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors to first responders, soldiers in battlefield scenarios, and beyond.

About the role:

As a member of the Product Design Team, you will work on meaningful projects that add value to Skydio and our users. You will solve complex, interesting problems and learn from a team of world-class engineers and researchers.

How you'll make an impact:

- Conquer challenges creatively with a scrappy mindset

- Design parts for next generation prototypes

- Chase down the root cause of mission critical issues on existing or developing products

- Find solutions with engineering design or manufacturing process changes

- Validate your solutions with hands-on prototyping, testing, and data collection

- Communicate with a cross functional team of engineers and suppliers around the globe

- Present your work in design reviews and learn from senior members of our team

What makes you a good fit:

- Relentless curiosity.

- Ability to leverage rock solid fundamentals to create exceptional designs for complicated products.

- Passion for elegant mechanical design at the highest and lowest levels of detail that will delight customers.

- Experience with 3D CAD. Familiarity with CATIA is highly valued.

- Obtaining FAA Part 107 certification within the first 60 days of employment is strongly encouraged for all Skydio employees and required for certain positions.

Bonus skills for the job (This experience is great to have, but we are also happy to teach you):

- How to design for a broad array of manufacturing processes including: injection molding, metal casting, CNC machining, sheet metal forming, and composites.

- How to complete DFM (design-for-manufacturing) with local and foreign suppliers

- How to design and integrate circuit boards, antennas, and connectors into mechanical assemblies

Some examples of past projects include:

- Gimbal Isolation: Design, simulate, re-design, DFM, and kick-off tooling for Skydio X10 gimbal vibration isolators

- Scrappy Wind Tunnel: Exactly what it sounds like. Research what it takes to make a wind tunnel. Build a wind tunnel. Use the wind tunnel to learn about aerodynamic forces on a drone to inform design improvements.

- Drone Battery Charger: Create prototypes for the battery charger for Skydio 2. Perform user studies, come up with a thermal solution, architect the product, and work on cosmetic surfacing.

What We Do

Gecko Robotics is helping the world’s most important organizations ensure the availability, reliability, and sustainability of critical infrastructure. Gecko's complete and connected solutions combine wall-climbing robots, industry-leading sensors, and an AI-powered data platform to provide customers with a unique window into the current and future health of their physical assets. This enables real-time decision making to increase the efficiency and safety of operations, promote mission readiness, and protect the environment and civilization from the effects of infrastructure failure.

Role at a Glance

Gecko Robotics is seeking a Software Engineering Intern to join RoboSPLAT within Field Infra in Pittsburgh for Summer 2027. This is a full-time, onsite internship, Monday through Friday.

RoboSPLAT builds software and tools that help teams develop, deploy, debug, and operate Gecko’s robotic and ultrasonic testing (UT) collection systems. You will work primarily in C/C++ and Python on a defined project that improves system integration, diagnostics, testing, or development workflows.

What you will do

- Develop C/C++ and Python software for a defined software project under the guidance of experienced engineers.

- Build or improve tooling, diagnostics, tests, or workflows that reduce friction in developing, debugging, and deploying software on robot hardware.

- Work across software and system boundaries by integrating services or hardware-facing interfaces, investigating system behavior, testing solutions, and documenting findings.

- Use version control, code review, and structured debugging practices to produce maintainable code.

- Collaborate with RoboSPLAT and partner teams, communicate status and tradeoffs clearly, and deliver a final demonstration and handoff.

Technologies We Use (If Applicable)

C/C++, Python, Git, Linux, networking, and ROS 2. Depending on the project, you may also work with the Yocto Project, NVIDIA Jetson Orin, cloud infrastructure, or Electron, React, and TypeScript.

About You

You are a hands-on engineering student who wants to understand how software behaves on real hardware. You work methodically, seek out missing knowledge, communicate clearly, and care about building tools and systems that others can use.

Required Skills

- Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related engineering discipline, with an expected graduation date between December 2027 and May 2028.

- Ability to work onsite in Pittsburgh, Monday through Friday, for the full Summer 2027 internship.

- Foundational programming experience in C/C++ and Python, including object-oriented programming.

- Working familiarity with Git or similar version control systems.

- Understanding of basic computer networking.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document technical work, explain findings and tradeoffs, and collaborate on ambiguous problems.

- Ability to independently close knowledge gaps, stay organized, and learn from feedback.

Preferred Skills

- Experience with ROS 2.

- Familiarity with embedded Linux systems or platforms such as the Yocto Project or NVIDIA Jetson Orin.

- Exposure to cloud infrastructure, preferably GCP.

- Experience building applications with Electron, React, or TypeScript.

- Exposure to embedded communication protocols, microcontrollers, or real-time operating systems is a plus.

- Ability to work with basic electronic systems, read simple schematics, and use common lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, and programmable power supplies.

Who We Are

At Gecko, our people are our greatest investment. In addition to competitive compensation packages, we offer company equity, 401(k) matching, gender-neutral parental leave, full medical, dental, and vision insurance, mental health, ongoing professional development, family planning assistance, and flexible paid time off.

Gecko values collaboration, innovation, and partnership, and we believe we do our best work when we're together in person. We’re an office-first culture but understand that sometimes you may need to work from home. Many people are in the office five days a week, others need a bit more flexibility. Ultimately, we care about the outcomes we achieve - and creating a culture of autonomy and trust that enables that impact.

Gecko is committed to creating a culture of inclusion and belonging, and we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe it is our collective responsibility to uphold these values and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to join us in our mission to protect today’s infrastructure and give form to tomorrow’s. All qualified applicants will be treated with respect and receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, uniform service, veteran status, age, or any other protected characteristic per federal, state, or local law. If you are passionate about what you do and want to use your talents to support our critical mission, we’d love to hear from you.
